tilts.set: SET on 2026-10-23 by the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting judg

industry.why: Neutral, carried, split. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): DNB Carnegie's new mining cycle and Danske's soft commodities up 10 to 40% since the second quarter are the demand side; Metals and mining relative strength falling to F from A, steel to D from B and cement to F from C are the tape, with energy costs at Brent $111 the margin squeeze. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, C prior. Base chemicals, Steel and Cement carry D; Fragrances, Specialty chemicals and Forestry stay C.

sector.key: M.10. Building materials - cement and aggregates
sector.why: Underweight, set deliberately this week (carried D from the old Basic materials and construction row). Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): cement and aggregates follow housing and construction, where Goldman Sachs (13-Oct) estimate each 100 basis points of higher rates cuts housing investment 6%, and the group is energy-intensive with European gas 'more than doubled'. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: F now, D prior, agrees. No MI Pool name. Counter-case: infrastructure and defence-funded spending supports part of the group, and rate-sensitive groups are where a relief rally starts; back to C if the Fed path is marked down.

geography.why: Underweight, carried unchanged with the reason strengthened. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the spillover from France to Italy is the new fact this week (Goldman, 16 Oct, 'tentative spillover to Italy'), and the Italian listings in the Pool are bank-heavy (Monte dei Paschi, Credito Emiliano, Mediobanca) beside global businesses (Eni, Saipem, Tenaris, STMicroelectronics, Technoprobe, Reply). Not Double Underweight because Goldman also says contagion risk is lower than in 2011-15, its fragmentation index shows risk 'remains limited', and Southern European banks are healthier; relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to F if the fragmentation index rises or the Italian premium is read above 150 basis points; back to C under 100.
